content:
{'translation': "Argentine's defense of the title, led by football king Messi, faces Spain, also beloved by Hong Kong people. The championship match kicks off at 3 AM today (the 20th), available on free-to-air television, yet large crowds of football-loving Hongkongers still took to the streets overnight, gathering at malls and bars to watch their beloved teams vie for the trophy.", 'translation_en': "Lionel Messi's Argentina, seeking to retain the title, take on Spain, another team beloved by Hong Kong fans. The final kicks off at 3am today (the 20th) and can be watched live on free-to-air TV, but large crowds of Hong Kong football fans still took to the streets overnight, heading to shopping malls and bars to watch their teams battle for the trophy."}

{'translation': 'Well before 3am, fans had already packed the venue at Olympian City, the atmosphere electrifying. Dressed in jerseys and waving the national flags and supporter items of their respective teams, they gathered to witness this once-every-four-years World Cup showdown.', 'translation_en': 'Long before 3am struck, fans had already packed the scene at Olympian City. Amid thunderous cheers, supporters wore their jerseys, held up the flags of their respective nations and brought their fan gear to welcome the World Cup final held once every four years.'}

{'translation': 'Spain dominated possession while Argentina held a solid defensive line. The first half ended goalless at 0-0. In the second half, Spain took control of the game, launching attacks with several threatening shots. In stoppage time, at the 92nd minute, Enzo Fernández received a second yellow card followed by a red and was sent off.', 'translation_en': 'Spain enjoyed more possession, while Argentina remained defensively steady. The first half ended 0-0. In the second half, Spain dictated the tempo and launched several threatening attacks. In stoppage time, at the 92nd minute, Enzo Fernández picked up a second yellow, resulting in a red card and his dismissal from the pitch.'}

{'translation': 'In the 96th minute, Spain won a free kick at the edge of the penalty area. Lamine Yamal took the shot, but Martínez saved it. The second-half score remained 0-0, with Argentina registering zero shots on target throughout the 90 minutes. The match went to extra time, with Argentina down to ten men. In the 95th minute of extra time, Nico Williams scored, but the goal was ruled out due to a prior foul by Merino.', 'translation_en': 'At the 96th minute, Spain earned a free kick at the top of the box. Yamal took the shot, and Martínez made the save. The score remained 0-0 after the second half, with Argentina failing to register a single shot in 90 minutes. The game went to extra time with Argentina playing with 10 men. In the 95th minute of extra time, Nico Williams found the net, but the goal was disallowed for a foul by Merino earlier in the play.'}

{'translation': "In the first half, Spain pressed Argentina hard, enjoying longer periods of possession, while Argentina defended resolutely. Argentina mounted occasional counterattacks, but failed to pose a significant threat to Spain before the water break. In the 38th minute, Spain's Oyarzabal fired a shot from the edge of the box but failed to break the deadlock. Around the 40th minute, Argentina's Lisandro Martínez received the first yellow card of the match.", 'translation_en': "In the first half, Spain pressed high and held possession for longer periods, while Argentina stayed compact defensively. Argentina attempted occasional counters but did not trouble Spain much before the water break. In the 38th minute, Spain's Oyarzabal shot from the edge of the box but could not find the net. Around the 40th minute, Argentina's Lisandro Martínez picked up the first yellow card."}

{'translation': 'Just after the start of the second half, Argentina\'s defence committed a costly mistake, allowing Spain\'s front line to win the ball high up the pitch, though they ultimately failed to convert the chance. In the 51st minute, a serious altercation broke out on the pitch. Argentina\'s Leandro pushed a Spanish player to the ground during the scuffle, prompting Spanish fans at the scene to become highly agitated and chant "Red card!"', 'translation_en': 'Right after the second half kicked off, Argentina\'s defence made a serious error, and Spain\'s front line won the ball back high up the pitch, but they could not find the net. In the 51st minute, a heated clash erupted on the pitch. Argentina\'s Leandro shoved a Spanish player to the ground during the scuffle, and Spanish fans in the stands, emotionally charged, shouted "Red card!"'}

{'translation': 'In the 59th minute, Spain won a free kick, but Argentina cleared the danger successfully. Spain made substitutions, bringing on Ferran Torres among others. In the 66th minute, Yamal crossed from the by-line, and Ferran Torres headed the ball on target, only for goalkeeper Martínez to gather it safely.', 'translation_en': 'In the 59th minute, Spain earned a free kick, and Argentina cleared it successfully. Spain brought on Ferran Torres and others. In the 66th minute, Yamal delivered a cross from the by-line, and Ferran Torres headed it on target, but the goalkeeper Martínez gathered the ball.'}

{'translation': 'Facing what was so far the closest chance of the match, Spanish fans at the scene could not help but shout "Ooh!" and "So close!", expressing deep regret that Spain failed to score, while also chanting "Well played!" to show their satisfaction with Spain\'s performance.', 'translation_en': 'Faced with what was the closest chance of the match so far, Spanish fans at the venue couldn\'t help but exclaim "Ooh!" and "So close!", lamenting the missed opportunity while also shouting "Well played!" to express satisfaction with Spain\'s performance.'}

{'translation': 'In the 82nd minute, Argentina\'s Enzo Fernández received a yellow card. During stoppage time in the 92nd minute, Enzo Fernández received a second yellow followed by a red, and was sent off. Some Spanish fans at the venue stood up and chanted "He deserves it!" and "Red card well deserved!", while Argentine fans on the other side expressed "That\'s debatable" and "Are you kidding me?", dissatisfied with the referee\'s decision.', 'translation_en': 'In the 82nd minute, Argentina\'s Enzo Fernández received a yellow card, and in the 92nd minute of stoppage time, he picked up a second yellow, resulting in a red card and his dismissal. Some Spanish fans in attendance stood up and shouted "He deserves it!" and "Red card well deserved!", while Argentine fans responded with "That\'s disputable" and "Are you serious?", unhappy with the referee\'s decision.'}

{'translation': 'During stoppage time, in the 96th minute, Spain won another free kick at the edge of the box. Yamal took the shot, and Martínez saved it. Facing Spain\'s fierce attacks, compounded by Argentina being reduced to ten men during stoppage time, the match — already dominated by Spain — became even more one-sided. Some Argentine fans shouted "Hold on!" in the hope that Argentina could hold out until the penalty shootout stage.', 'translation_en': 'In the 96th minute of stoppage time, Spain won another free kick at the top of the box. Yamal shot and Martínez saved it. Facing Spain\'s relentless attacking pressure and Argentina being a man down after the red card in stoppage time, the match — already dominated by Spain — became even more one-sided. Some Argentine fans shouted "Hold the line!", hoping Argentina could survive until the penalty shootout.'}

{'translation': 'In the 95th minute of extra time, Nico Williams found the net. Some Spanish fans rushed to the big screen to celebrate, but the goal was ruled out for a prior foul by Merino. Not until the 105th minute, when Spanish fans once again rushed to the screen to set off confetti cannons and celebrate, chanting "Let\'s go!" and "Finally!"', 'translation_en': 'In the 95th minute of extra time, Nico Williams scored, prompting some Spanish fans to rush to the big screen in celebration, but the goal was disallowed for a foul by Merino earlier in the move. It was not until the 105th minute that Spanish fans once again rushed to the screen, setting off confetti and celebrating wildly, chanting "Let\'s go!" and "Finally!"'}

{'translation': 'Ultimately, Spain defeated Argentina 1-0. Large crowds of Spanish fans, "young and old alike", all dressed in Spain jerseys, raised replica World Cup trophies together and cheered in celebration.', 'translation_en': 'Spain ultimately defeated Argentina 1-0, and large crowds of Spanish fans, "young and old", all dressed in Spanish jerseys, raised replica FIFA World Cup trophies together and cheered in celebration.'}

{'translation': 'Spanish fan Mr. Yuan believed Spain\'s performance in the final was "quite good — they just played their normal game", but felt that "the final touch was still a bit lacking", as they failed to capitalise on numerous chances.', 'translation_en': 'Spanish fan Mr. Yuan felt Spain\'s performance in the final was "pretty good — they just played their usual game", but noted that "the finishing touch was still a bit off", having failed to convert several opportunities.'}

{'translation': 'Argentine fan Mr. Cao also hoped that broadcast events for major matches such as the Champions League final or other cup competitions could be held in the future, believing that such large-scale screening events would "definitely have an even better atmosphere". As for Argentina\'s performance in the final, Mr. Cao said: "I\'m satisfied with this tournament." He had not expected before the World Cup that Argentina "could reach the final stage again", and felt that Argentina\'s spirit of unity remained strong — "it\'s the team that holds this Argentina squad together".', 'translation_en': 'Argentine fan Mr. Cao also expressed hope that future broadcast events for major matches such as the Champions League final or other cup competitions could be held, believing that "the atmosphere would definitely be even better" for such large-scale football screening events. Regarding Argentina\'s performance in the final, Mr. Cao said: "I\'m satisfied with this tournament." He had not expected before the World Cup that Argentina "could make it to the final again", and felt that Argentina\'s togetherness remained strong — "it\'s the team spirit that holds this Argentina side together."'}
